title: Count people, not percentages
summary: A 90% accurate test on a 1% condition: build the table of 10,000 people and find how many positives are really sick.

blocks.title: How many are sick?

define.meaning: The share of people who have the condition. Here $\frac{1}{100}$.
The test says “you have it”. A positive can be right or wrong.

blocks.why: Probabilities are easy to misread. Counting people is not. Start the table with the smallest group.
blocks.prompt: A condition affects 1% of people. Out of 10,000 people, how many have it?

slips.say: That is 1% of 100. The group is 10,000 people.
That is the healthy group. The question asks for the sick one.

check.say: The sick and the healthy must add to 10,000.

blocks.title: Sick and tested positive

define.meaning: The share of sick people the test flags: $P(\text{positive} \mid \text{sick})$.

blocks.why: The test catches most, not all, of the sick. This is the first of the two groups that test positive.
blocks.prompt: The test is positive for 90% of people who have the condition (its **sensitivity**). Of the 100 sick people, how many test positive?

slips.say: That is the sick people the test misses. You want those it catches.
That is 90% of all 10,000. Only the 100 sick people can be true positives.

hints: Take 90% of the sick group, not of everyone.

blocks.title: Healthy and tested positive

define.meaning: The share of healthy people the test flags by mistake: $P(\text{positive} \mid \text{healthy})$.

blocks.why: A small error rate on a big group is a big number of people. This is why rare conditions surprise.
blocks.prompt: The test is also positive for 5% of healthy people (the **false positive rate**). There are 9,900 healthy people. How many test positive?

slips.say: That is 5% of 10,000. Only the 9,900 healthy people can be false positives.
That is 5% of the 100 sick. False alarms come from the healthy group.

check.say: Compare with the 90 true positives. Which group is bigger?

blocks.title: Positive: how likely is sick?
blocks.why: This is the number a patient wants. It is a share of the positives, not of the sick.
blocks.prompt: Of 10,000 people, 100 are sick. Of those, 90 test positive. Of the 9,900 healthy people, 495 test positive. Someone tests positive. What fraction of all positives are sick? Give a fraction.

slips.say: That is the share of the sick who test positive, the other way round. Here you divide by all positives.
That compares the 90 with the 495 only. The positives are $90 + 495$.
That divides by all 10,000 people. Divide by the 585 who tested positive.

hints: First count everyone who tests positive.
$90 + 495 = 585$ positives. How many of them are sick?

check.say: It should be well below 1/2: false alarms outnumber true positives.

blocks.solution: $\frac{90}{585} = \frac{2}{13}$, about 15%. A positive result from a 90% test means about a 15% chance, because the condition is rare. Next lesson names this idea.
